title: Emergency Operations Land Assessments
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in support of the Federal Emergency Management Agency was task to conduct Land Assessments for potential Temporary Housing Units in areas of Florida recently effected by Hurricane Irma. Stephen H. Harris, team lead quality assurance, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Huntington District, and Ron Saunders, quality assurance, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Huntington District, discuss the mission and how residents are responding. (Video by: Hector Mosley, public affairs, USACE, New York District)
keywords: FEMA, temporary housing, Monroe County, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Jacksonville District, USACE New York District, Hurricane Irma, USACE Emergency Operations, Keys Strong, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Emergency Operations, U.S. Army
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District

transcript.text: Our mission here in Florida is to go out and find sites that we can possibly put RV trailers
in so people can get temporary housing.
We're doing temporary housing assessments because these people were devastated by the
recent hurricane that came through here.
Like this home here had about three feet of water on the living area and their homes are
totally destroyed and going to be demoed.
So we're trying to come up with some sort of temporary housing so they can survive
until they get something else built back.
When we come to a piece of property we look at the site to see if it's even feasible to
put a trailer on there like the debris is gone, if the utilities are on to make sure
they're with electric water and so we're hooked up and ready to go.
And if they're still interested in getting a temporary structure we do what we can to
help them get the paperwork filed and we send it up to FEMA or let them know that the site
is feasible for its temporary trailer.
The response when you pull up on sites are very welcoming.
People are looking for some sort of hope and I think that's what we give them is a little
bit of hope that assistance is coming.
And personally I've been on several of these and anything we can do to try and help these
folks that are so devastated is good.
It's great that we have a job that we have a chance to come down and help people like
this so very gratifying.
The people down here one thing I noticed that everyone we encountered are very grateful
we're here and to be what they've gone through they're very giving people very giving people
down here.
I mean they'll do anything in the world for you and see what they've been through it just
makes your heart, makes you feel warm inside.
It's always a pleasure to come down and try and help and get people back on their feet.
Everyone is so grateful and all the local people that we talk to the politicians everybody
I think is very thankful that we're here.
I hope we don't have any more disasters but if we do then I'll be here to assist however
I can.
